name: MonarchAiToolApproval
title: AiToolApproval
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with a VStack of Text, MonarchBadge for the risk, MonarchFormField around a vertical TextField for the JSON and the reason, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) for Always allow, and Buttons with .buttonStyle(.monarch(…)) in a MonarchFlowLayout; @AccessibilityFocusState for the first focus
summary: The approval card for a tool call the assistant wants to run: what it will do, its arguments as readable pairs, the risk, and Approve and Deny, with editable arguments, an optional reason and an optional Always allow.
whenToUse: In an assistant conversation, for each tool-call part in the pending-approval state, before the app runs the tool.
whenNotToUse: After the decision, to show what ran, use MonarchAiToolCall. To grant an assistant standing permissions use MonarchAiPermissionScope. For a confirmation that is not about a tool call use a confirmationDialog.
api: init(_ part: MonarchAiToolCallPart, summary: String? = nil, consequence: String? = nil, risk: MonarchAiToolCallRisk? = nil, toolLabels: [String: String] = [:], argumentLabels: [String: String] = [:], argumentOrder: [String] = [], isEditable: Bool = true, focusesOnAppear: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels = MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels(), onAlwaysAllow: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onDeny: @escaping @MainActor (String?) -> Void, onApprove: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchAiJSON?) -> Void)

options.name: part
options.description: The tool call waiting for a decision (state .pendingApproval). A new id starts the card over.

options.name: summary
options.description: The title in plain words, such as "Delete 12 records". The tool's label by default.

options.name: consequence
options.description: What happens if this is approved. Destructive calls say "This can’t be undone once it runs." by default.

options.name: risk
options.description: How much harm approving can do: low, medium, high or destructive. The call's own risk, else medium.

options.name: toolLabels
options.description: Display names by tool name. Unlisted tools get a humanized name.

options.name: argumentLabels
options.description: Labels for argument keys, such as ["to": "Recipients"]. Unlisted keys are humanized.

options.name: isEditable
options.description: Offers Edit arguments, a JSON editor.

options.name: focusesOnAppear
options.description: Moves VoiceOver focus to Deny (high and destructive) or Approve when the card appears.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the risk names, the consequence and the announcement.

options.name: onAlwaysAllow
options.description: Shows "Always allow this tool". When ticked, called with the tool name just before onApprove. Never offered for destructive calls.

options.name: onDeny
options.description: Called when the person denies, with the trimmed reason, or nil.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Called when the person approves, with the edited input, or nil when the arguments were not changed.

states.name: pending
states.description: The header (warning icon, "Approval needed", title, risk badge), the arguments and the buttons.

states.name: low, medium, high
states.description: Neutral, warning and warning badge tones; Approve is the primary button.

states.name: destructive
states.description: Danger tone, the consequence line, no Always allow, and Approve is the danger button.

states.name: editing
states.description: A JSON editor with the pretty-printed input; Edit arguments becomes Discard edits.

states.name: invalid JSON
states.description: Approve does nothing and "Fix the JSON before approving." shows under the editor with an icon.

states.name: reason
states.description: Add a reason opens a reason field; its text is passed to onDeny.

states.name: approved, denied, cancelled
states.description: The buttons give way to the outcome with a check, a cross or a minus, also when the call's state is no longer pending.

appearance: A Monarch card on the surface colour with an extra-small elevation. The header icon and consequence use the strong warning or danger roles by risk, the eyebrow and keys are muted text, the risk is a subtle badge in its tone, and the outcome uses the strong success or danger role or muted text. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web renders a group with a description list and an assertive live region; iOS uses a MonarchCard, a VStack of label and value pairs (sorted by key, because MonarchAiJSON objects have no order) and an AccessibilityNotification announcement. The web's focusOnMount moves keyboard focus; iOS's focusesOnAppear moves VoiceOver focus. The web's describe returns any content; iOS takes a summary String. The JSON editor is a vertical TextField that reuses the action editor's bordered field until a shared multi-line field exists. The web keeps the card focusable after the decision; on iOS the outcome line is a plain element. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The header is one element read as "Approval needed", the title and the risk, with the header trait.
"Approval needed: <title>" is announced when a pending card appears.
With focusesOnAppear, VoiceOver focus moves to Deny for high and destructive calls and to Approve otherwise.
Each argument is one element read as its label and value.
The JSON and reason fields are labelled through MonarchFormField; the JSON error is text with an icon and is announced.
The risk and the outcome are words with icons, not only colours.
Every button and the checkbox are at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A string input that is not an object is shown as code; a nested value is shown as pretty JSON.
Approving with the editor open but unchanged passes nil, like the web.
A part whose state is not pendingApproval shows its outcome at once and is not announced.
Long titles and values wrap; the buttons wrap onto more rows at large text sizes.

examples.title: Send an email
examples.template:
MonarchAiToolApproval(
    MonarchAiToolCallPart(
        id: {{call.id}},
        name: {{call.name}},
        input: [
            "to": [{{call.to.0}}, {{call.to.1}}, {{call.to.2}}],
            "subject": {{call.subject}},
            "body": {{call.body}},
        ],
        state: .pendingApproval
    ),
    summary: {{summary}},
    argumentOrder: ["to", "subject", "body"],
    onAlwaysAllow: { _ in },
    onDeny: { _ in },
    onApprove: { _ in }
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiToolApproval(
    MonarchAiToolCallPart(
        id: "send-1",
        name: "send_email",
        input: [
            "to": ["alex@example.test", "kim@example.test", "sam@example.test"],
            "subject": "Weekly update",
            "body": "Hi all, the weekly update is attached.",
        ],
        state: .pendingApproval
    ),
    summary: "Send email to 3 people",
    argumentOrder: ["to", "subject", "body"],
    onAlwaysAllow: { _ in },
    onDeny: { _ in },
    onApprove: { _ in }
)
